JUST DANCE 2.0

SCROLL INTO THE STORY
01

THE ORIGIN // LOVE THE MUSIC

K-POP MADE ME
WANT TO MOVE.

I really love K-pop. I have seen BLACKPINK, ITZY, Stray Kids, aespa, BIBI, and more live—and every show made the choreography feel as essential as the music.

I wanted to learn those dances for myself: not just copy the outline of a move, but understand the timing, shape, and energy that made it land.

LIVE MEMORY // CONCERT LOG
  • BLACKPINK
  • ITZY
  • STRAY KIDS
  • AESPA
  • BIBI
AND THE PLAYLIST KEEPS GROWING.
02
“A replay could show me the move.
It could not tell me what I was doing wrong.”

THE GAP // FEEDBACK IS THE HARD PART

I NEEDED A TEACHER
IN THE ROOM.

Learning alone always hit the same wall. I could slow a video down and repeat a sequence, but I still needed someone in person to spot the details I could not see.

Was I early? Were my arms too low? Did my posture collapse? Which move should I repeat?
03

THE BUILD // TURN MOTION INTO SIGNAL

SO I BUILT A COACH
THAT WATCHES BACK.

Just Dance 2.0 follows the performance through a camera, aligns it with reference choreography, and turns movement into feedback you can act on.

POSE LOCK // 33 KEYPOINTS
  1. 01REFERENCE

    Load the choreography or movement you want to learn.

  2. 02TRACK

    Map the dancer into a live pose skeleton on device.

  3. 03ALIGN

    Compare corresponding movement across time, not just one frozen frame.

  4. 04COACH

    Return a score and identify the next correction to practice.

04

THE COACH // NOT JUST A NUMBER

GRADE THE MOVE.
TEACH THE NEXT ONE.

A useful score has to explain itself. The assistant separates timing, arms, legs, and posture so the next practice run has a clear target.

LOCAL BY DESIGN — the desktop workflow can run offline, keeping the camera loop immediate and private.

PERFORMANCE ANALYSISDEMO SESSION

NEXT CORRECTION

Lift the left elbow through the transition and land the final count half a beat later.

05

BEYOND K-POP // ANY MOVEMENT CAN TEACH BACK

THE DANCE WAS
JUST THE BEGINNING.

The same idea works for any workout you are trying to learn. If a movement has form, timing, and a repeatable reference, the assistant can watch the attempt and give feedback.
